extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum theorists, teachers, and students of education
extracted.subtask_description: Framework of criteria for selecting, presenting, and valuing curricular subject matter (especially science, arts, and experiential activities) in democratic education. Emphasizes how science, direct experience, imagination, and appreciation should shape teaching and curriculum design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning over rote knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "Knowing the definitions, rules, formulae, etc., is like knowing the names of parts of a machine without knowing what they do."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual content is what an element accomplishes in the system of which it is a member — teach for function, use, and connected meaning rather than isolated facts or names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science as agent of social progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Science "marks the emancipation of mind from devotion to customary purposes and makes possible the systematic pursuit of new ends."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present science as the means of projecting new possibilities and shaping ends (examples: industrial inventions, control of disease, prospects for reducing poverty); treat scientific knowledge as central to social progress, not merely technical improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use science to modify aims and imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Education has the responsibility of using science to modify the habitual attitude of imagination and feeling, not leave it just an extension of our physical arms and legs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid teaching science solely as technical means; integrate it so it reshapes purposes and quality of human aims and desires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach science as humanistic knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: For educational purposes, natural science is knowledge of the conditions of human action and is thoroughly humanistic in quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid opposing science and humanities; show how scientific knowledge contributes to understanding human affairs, interdependence, and democratic life, rather than treating 'applied' knowledge as inferior to 'pure' theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating scientific instruction as mere formal exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching science merely as a set of formal and technical exercises makes it an end in itself and fails to procure culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context and meaning so scientific instruction serves humanistic ends; do not reduce science teaching to technical drills or disconnected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide direct experience before symbolic instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Before teaching through signs and symbolic media, schooling must provide genuine situations in which personal participation brings home the import of the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use play and active occupations to supply the background of realization/appreciation; ensure students have first‑hand, quality experiences that connect to later symbolic learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory work to give 'feeling' before technique
rubrics_metrics.description: The first basic function of laboratory work is to familiarize the student at first hand with a range of facts and problems — to give him a 'feeling' for them; mastery of technique is secondary at first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design lab and practical work to build appreciation and intuition before emphasizing formal methods and technical proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstraction and generalization as essential scientific traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstraction detaches what is common in experience so it may be saved for further use; generalization is the application/extension of that abstraction to new experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and value the processes of abstraction, generalization, and definite formulation because they free experience from accidental particulars and make knowledge socially shareable and practically useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation is essential to thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and propositions record, fix, and convey what is abstracted; formulation is not an after‑thought but essential to completing the work of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize precise expression and terminology so intellectual tools can be communicated and applied by others; encourage students to formulate ideas explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish appreciating realization from mere representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciative realizations (direct, imaginative, personal responses) are qualitatively different from symbolic or representative experiences which can be remote or merely formal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster personal, imaginative engagement that makes symbolic material meaningful; avoid letting symbols become ends in themselves (bookishness or academic detachment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as medium of appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a personal response involving imagination can procure realization even of pure 'facts'; imagination translates symbols into direct meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat play, manual activities, and laboratory exercises as imaginative enterprises; design activities to stimulate imaginative concern so learning is not mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts fix taste and intensify appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature, music, drawing, painting, etc., enhance the qualities that make experience appealing and serve to fix taste and standards for later experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include fine arts not as luxuries but as central means to develop heightened appreciation, standards of quality, and demands for better conditions; use arts to reveal deeper meanings in ordinary experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of valuation must be realized, not merely taught
rubrics_metrics.description: Working standards of value depend upon what an individual has himself specifically appreciated in concrete situations, not merely on verbal instruction about values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create opportunities for students to personally experience qualities (e.g., kindness, clarity, harmony) so their professed standards become authentic and operative rather than merely symbolic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on merely empirical (crude) practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary 'empirical' (crudely empirical) methods are happy‑go‑lucky and lend themselves to deception; experimental science means reason operating within experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote experimental, reflective methods that use past experience as servant of reason rather than slavishly imitating past practice; guard against quackery and routine imitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject a fixed hierarchy of studies; value is situational
rubrics_metrics.description: It is futile to establish a hierarchy of values among studies; many values are intrinsic and incomparable, and valuation appears when choices make some studies means to other ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that educational value is contextual and tied to life; curriculum decisions should not rest on absolute rank of subjects but on their contribution to living and situational ends.
